title: Link the enabler to other documents
prompt:
# Story 6: Link the enabler to other documents

- **Story**: XXX-link-enabler
- **Created**: 2026-11-08
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: draft an enabler, link a driver and another enabler with the Link button, see their chips, and see the draft use what they say;
  approve it and open its links from the file.

## Story

As a team member, I want to link the enabler to the drivers and other enablers that shape it, so that the AI uses what they say, and the
connection is kept with the enabler.

## Acceptance tests

Choosing links

- [ ] **Given** the prompt, **Then** a button "Link" (with a link icon) sits under the box. **When** the user presses it, **Then** a list
  opens (`role="dialog"`, "Choose what to link") above or below it, groups it by kind with the headings "Drivers", "Architectural
  enablers" and "Stories", and shows a checkbox and the label of each document.
- [ ] **Given** an enabler prompt, **Then** the ADRs are **not** in the list: they are chosen as chips in the green panel (story 1).
- [ ] **Given** a driver, **Then** it is listed whether or not it has text. **Given** nothing to link, **Then** the list says "Nothing to
  link yet."
- [ ] **Given** a document is checked, **Then** the button shows a count, and a chip with its icon and label appears above the box, with a
  button "Remove link to <label>". **When** the user removes the chip, **Then** it is unchecked.
- [ ] **Given** the list is open, **When** the user presses Escape or clicks outside it, **Then** it closes and the choice stays.
- [ ] **Given** the user sends, **Then** the links are cleared from the composer, as the text is.
- [ ] **Given** a draft, **Then** the card shows the chips of the ADRs and of the links, and they cannot be changed there. **Given** a revision
  (story 4), **Then** the Link button is not shown.

What the model gets

- [ ] **Given** links, **Then** the request has "## Linked documents (full text)" and, for each document, "### <label> (<relation>, <path>)"
  and its full text, cut at 12,000 characters. The ADRs it derives from come first, with the relation "derives from", then the others with
  "linked". A document is listed once.
- [ ] **Given** a linked enabler, **Then** the request also brings, with it, the ADRs it derives from ("derived from by the linked AE-0001...")
  and the enablers and stories it links to ("linked from the linked AE-0001..."), one step only, not the document itself.
- [ ] **Given** no link, **Then** the section reads "## Linked documents" and "- None" (and the ADRs it derives from are listed in full).
- [ ] **Given** the system prompt, **Then** it tells the model to treat the linked documents as context and to cite one only when a rule
  comes from it, for example (Driver: Constraints).

Keeping them

- [ ] **Given** approval, **Then** the links are stored with the enabler (not the ADRs, which are kept as the ones it derives from), and the
  message says "It is linked to N other items."
- [ ] **Given** the open enabler, **Then** "Linked to" shows a chip for each, and each chip opens that file. **Given** the file it links to,
  **Then** it shows the enabler under "Referenced by".
- [ ] **Given** a document that is removed later, **Then** a link to it is hidden, not an error.

## Business rules and constraints

- The model sees the **outgoing** links only: what the enabler links to and the ADRs it derives from. Documents that merely link to it are
  not sent.
- Only one step is followed through a linked enabler, and never through a story, a driver or an ADR.
- A reference is a stable text: `driver:constraints`, `enabler:0001-set-up-...`, `story:...` and `adr:0006`. It comes from the name of the
  file, never from a random id.
- An enabler's links are chosen when it is drafted. Changing them afterwards is another story.

## Out of scope

- Adding or removing links of an approved enabler, the *Cross enabler* flag (a cross enabler would be linked to every new story, and does
  nothing for an enabler), and links between stories.
- Showing the links of a document as a graph.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add the Link button and its list to the composer, grouped by kind, without the ADRs, with the count and the removable chips.
- [ ] Add the links to the draft and the card, and to the stored enabler without the ADRs.
- [ ] Put the linked documents in the request: derives from first, linked after, once each, cut at 12,000 characters.
- [ ] Add the documents reached through a linked enabler, one step.
- [ ] Show "Referenced by" in the read-only panel for the documents that are linked from an enabler.
- [ ] Test: the list and its kinds, no ADR in it, the chips, the request with and without links, the cut, the one step, and a removed target.

tasks.text: Add the Link button and dialog to the enabler composer: grouped by kind (Drivers, Architectural enablers, Stories), no ADRs, with checkboxes, count badge, and removable chips above the prompt box (ADR-0007, AE-0002).
Wire the dialog open/close behaviour: Escape and outside-click close it while preserving selection; chips clear on submit.
Display link chips on the draft card alongside ADR chips, read-only; hide the Link button from the revision prompt (story 027).

Extend the backend request builder to assemble "## Linked documents (full text)": derives-from ADRs first, then linked documents, each truncated at 12,000 characters, each appearing once (ADR-0017, AE-0005).
Implement one-step transitive expansion for linked enablers: include their derives-from ADRs and their own links, without recursing further (ADR-0017).
Update the system-prompt template to instruct the model to treat linked documents as context and cite them only when a rule comes from them.
Persist the chosen links (excluding derives-from ADRs) on the enabler aggregate in `bwyn-core`; expose them via the approval command in `bwyn-application` (ADR-0017, AE-0005).
Add the confirmation message "It is linked to N other items." to the approval response (story 026).
Render "Linked to" chips in the read-only file panel and "Referenced by" on the panels of linked documents; suppress missing-document chips silently (AE-0002).

Write Jest tests: dialog grouping, ADR absence, chip add/remove, request assembly with and without links, 12,000-character truncation, one-step transitive expansion, and silent handling of a removed link target (ADR-0005, ADR-0016).

Write a JUnit test asserting that the link-persistence command and the transitive-expansion query reside in the correct hexagonal layers and that no domain class references adapter types (ADR-0009, ADR-0017).

Extend the backend request builder to assemble "## Linked documents": the linked documents in the order chosen (or "- None"), each with its relation and path, truncated at 12,000 characters, each appearing once; implement `FetchLinkedDocumentsPort` with the project's drivers, enablers and ADRs in place of the placeholder adapter (ADR-0017, AE-0005).

Write Jest tests: dialog grouping, ADR absence, chip add/remove, the links sent with the first draft, a change and a retry, the links sent with the approval, "Linked to" with a removed target left out silently, and "Referenced by" (ADR-0005, ADR-0016). Write JUnit tests for the request with and without links, the 12,000-character truncation, one-step transitive expansion, and the adapter against the database (ADR-0005, ADR-0012).
Write a JUnit test asserting that the linked-documents port is implemented only by an outbound adapter and that no domain class references adapter types (ADR-0009, ADR-0017).
